subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: Generic runtime support routines with no attested owner: 3DNow/MMX packed-float kernels (cubic-Bezier-style interpolation, a partial quaternion product, a normalized perpendicular/cross direction), an allocator-descriptor callback contract plus the resource-buffer allocation/free lifecycle built on it, an MPEG bitstream/header-processing cluster sharing the CMpegBase_ProcessHeader callee, a zlib-style inflate/deflate codec (fast-path inflate, buffered stream read, Adler-32, longest-match, Huffman tree construction, rank redistribution, canonical code assignment), and a set of orphaned global-flag/ROM-copy/import-thunk helpers. The grouping is a DERIVED synthesis from shared callees, shared descriptor layouts and shared intrinsic flavor in the packet, not an attested source organization.

summary: The packet covers 26 functions across six weakly-related runtime object clusters, all but one with UNKNOWN owners. The 3DNow/MMX cluster provides cubic-Bezier-style interpolation, a partial quaternion product and a normalized cross/perpendicular direction as freestanding packed-float kernels with read-only constant globals. An allocator-descriptor pattern (allocation callback +0x20, release callback +0x24, handle +0x28) backs the resource-buffer alloc/free lifecycle, a 28-byte object allocation with field fill, a generic indirect-dispatch helper and a free wrapper. An MPEG bitstream cluster shares the callee CMpegBase_ProcessHeader and the bitstream-buffer fields at this+0x24A4/0x24F0, plus a vtable I/O read at *(this+0x2D34)+8. A zlib-style codec cluster covers the inflate fast path, a buffered stream read, Adler-32, the deflate longest-match search, and the Huffman tree construction/rank-redistribution/canonical-code-assignment trio. The remainder are orphaned helpers: a global-flag stub trampoline, the fatal-halt handler, a two-global pointer swap, a ROM-to-RAM interleaved table copy, an AVI import thunk and a string-length dispatch. All classes here are synthetic groupings inferred from shared evidence; ownership and most field semantics remain UNKNOWN.

function_roles.role: 3DNow! cubic-Bezier-style interpolation between four packed float control points (a2..a5) parameterized by scalar factor a6: broadcast the factor, derive higher-order weight coefficients with packed multiply/add/difference/sign-flip operations (packed [2.0f,3.0f] scale, 0x8000000000000000 sign flip), blend the first packed element of all four inputs and the full second packed element, scale both results by packed 0.5f, emit EMMS and return the output pointer a1.

3DNow partial quaternion product: packed-multiplies the first component pairs of a2/a3, accumulates a dot-product-like term from the second-pair low dwords, copies the a3 first pair to output a1[0], stores the sign-flipped accumulated value (XOR 0x80000000, global qword_5AF978) into a1[1].high, and clears 3DNow/MMX state with _m_femms at entry and exit.

3DNow normalized perpendicular/cross direction computed from differences of three input vectors (a2..a4): assemble cross-style perpendicular terms, compute a squared length, normalize with a Newton-refined guarded reciprocal square root against a denormal epsilon threshold, force the output pair to zero at or below the guard, and write the normalized direction pair to a1 with a sign flip on the second lane.

Allocate and initialize a resource buffer struct through an allocator object: use the allocation callback at this+0x20 with the handle at this+0x28 to allocate the primary struct (size 64), a secondary fixed buffer (tag 8, size 1440) and a variable buffer (tag 1, size a3); on success store the buffers at v3[9]/v3[10], set v3[0]=0, v3[11]=a3+size, v3[14]=a2, call sub_52765A to reset it and return the struct; on any allocation failure release prior blocks through the callback at this+0x24 and return 0.

Reset resource state via sub_52765A(a1, a2, 0), then invoke the indirect release callback (function pointer at a2+0x24, context dword at a2+0x28) three times passing the variable buffer (a1+0x28), the secondary buffer (a1+0x24) and the a1 struct itself, and return 0.

Dispatch through the function pointer at (a5+0x20) with the value at (a5+0x28), 1 and 28; if the returned object is non-null, zero its first dword and store two bytes (offsets +0x10, +0x11) and two dwords (offsets +0x14, +0x18) from a1..a4, then return the object pointer (possibly null).

Indirect-call dispatch helper: load the function pointer stored at a2+0x24 and the argument dword at a2+0x28, call the pointer with (arg, a1), and return the callee result; a vtable- or callback-table-style dispatch site.

Read four global base pointers (dword_5D9418, dword_5D941C, address of unk_5D9420, address of unk_5DA420) into the four caller-provided output parameters and return 0; consumed by the audio-codec initialization caller sub_527752.

DEFLATE fast-path decoder (zlib inflate_fast equivalent): decode literal/length and distance Huffman codes from the bit stream, emit literals into the circular output window and copy length-distance matches with wraparound while at least 0x102 window bytes and 0xA bits remain, using the dword_5DA520 bit-mask table and the per-table node layout; write 'invalid distance code'/'invalid literal/length code' into the stream error slot and return 1 (block complete), 0 (ran out of window/input) or -3 (invalid code).

Decode one MPEG audio frame header from the bitstream: snapshot the bit position to this+0x24A8, read a byte-swapped 32-bit sync word from the buffer at this+0x24A4 (fallback to the default header word at this+0x24F0 when no buffer is set), validate via CMpegBase_ProcessHeader, and on success advance the bit position at this+0x24AC by 8 * frame_size_bytes(this+0x2498) + 32; return 0 on a valid header, -1 otherwise.

Read a 4-byte word from the I/O interface object at this+0x2D34 via its vtable read function at slot +8 (args &v3, 4, 0), byte-swap the value and forward it to CMpegBase_ProcessHeader(this, v3); return 0 when the header is accepted, -1 when CMpegBase_ProcessHeader returned -1.

Read the next MPEG sync word from the buffer pointer at this+0x24A4 (fallback to the default header word at this+0x24F0 when the buffer is null), byte-swap it and pass it to CMpegBase_ProcessHeader; return TRUE (1) when the header is invalid (-1), FALSE (0) when accepted.
Conditional trampoline: read the global flag dword_8B0108 and, when it is non-zero, invoke EmptyStub_0170 (an empty stub per its name); no return value and no other side effects.

Fatal-halt entry point: invoke the global halt-handler function pointer off_5DA714 (static graph target sub_52E4E0) with the message string aHaltingProgram, then trap with __debugbreak() if the handler returns; return the value produced by the handler call.

Bounds-checked byte store: write the byte a3 into the receiver byte array at index a2 only when a2 <= 8 (fixed 9-element bound) and always return the original index; used by BufferInitZero as the per-byte fill step of a small fixed-size buffer.

Straight-line pointer copy: save the current value of dword_8B0110 into the return register, write dword_8B0118 as the first dword of the buffer addressed by dword_8B0110, and return the old pointer; the raw body only proves an old-pointer/new-pointer swap in a two-dword relationship.

Copy two fixed-size lookup tables from ROM into a single runtime buffer at unk_8B1924 with an interleaved 32-byte-block pattern: 16*15 blocks of 32 bytes from unk_5B6F0C (offsets j-i, j in {0..896 step 64}, i in {0..30 step 2}), then 16*17 blocks from unk_5B730C (offsets m-k, m in {0..1024 step 64}, k in {0..30 step 2}); call a no-op stub first and return an incidental offset value.

Import thunk for the AVIFileExit AVI library routine: unconditionally forward to the import address table entry __imp_AVIFileExit at 0x0059E04C and return; no parameters and no explicit body beyond the indirection.

String-aware dispatch helper: measure the length of the NUL-terminated string a2 via strlen and forward (a1, a2, length) to BufferFillWithTimeout, returning its result; called by ResourceLookupWithDualPath.

Buffered decompression-stream read: read up to a3 bytes clamped to the available bytes at stream+4, advance the buffer pointer at stream+0 and the total-read counter at stream+8, and when the flag at *(*(stream+28)+24) is clear run consumption bookkeeping through sub_537D10 storing its result at stream+48; return the number of bytes actually read.

LZ77 longest-match search over a hash chain: read window and chain parameters from the deflate state a1, walk the prev-hash chain from candidate a2, probe candidates with a prefix comparison, extend matches byte-by-byte with an 8-byte unrolled loop, record the best match origin and length in the state, and return the best length clamped to the lookahead.
Single-argument free-style wrapper: forward the pointer a2 to sub_58AA6F and return that callee's result; the first parameter a1 is accepted but not used.

Adler-32 checksum (classic zlib): a1 is the rolling 16-bit checksum pair (s1 low word, s2 high word), a2 the input buffer, a3 the byte count; process chunks of at most 5552 bytes with a 16-byte unrolled accumulation loop plus a residual loop, reducing both sums modulo 0xFFF1 after each chunk, and return s1 | (s2 << 16); called by DecompressionStreamRead.

Build an optimal Huffman prefix-code tree from a symbol frequency table: collect the non-zero-frequency symbols into a node-index array, synthesize dummy symbols when fewer than 2 remain, heapify and repeatedly combine the two smallest nodes into a parent (summing frequencies, taking max code length + 1), finalize the root, call RankRedistribution to enforce the maximum code length, and return the result of FrequencyTableConstruction which generates the canonical codes.

Maximum code-length enforcement pass of deflate-style Huffman tree construction: walk the tree node-index heap to derive each symbol's code length from its parent depth, clamp lengths above the maximum and count the overflow, redistribute the overflow by moving leaves shallower, and recompute every overlong symbol's length down to the limit while accumulating dynamic and static bit costs; invoked by HuffmanTreeConstructor.

Deflate-style canonical Huffman code assignment: phase 1 builds a per-length next-code table by advancing a running base code for each length against the symbol-count histogram and doubling; phase 2 walks symbols assigning the next code for each non-zero code length, transforms it through sub_539670, and writes the code word at a1+4*i; returns the last transformed code value.

classes.name: Simd3DNowVectorMath
classes.responsibility: Synthetic grouping of the three 3DNow/MMX packed-float kernels in this packet: a cubic-Bezier-style interpolation between four control-point pairs, a partial quaternion product, and a normalized perpendicular/cross direction computed from vector differences. Members share the two-__m64-lane convention at this+0x0/this+0x8, the read-only constant globals in the 0x005AF9xx range and _m_femms state hygiene; the class boundary is inferred from the shared 3DNow intrinsic flavor, not from owner evidence (all owners UNKNOWN).

classes.name: ResourceBufferAllocator
classes.responsibility: Synthetic grouping of the allocator-descriptor callbacks and the resource-buffer lifecycle helpers in this packet. The descriptor carries an allocation callback at +0x20, a release callback at +0x24 and a handle/context dword at +0x28. ResourceBufferAllocInit allocates and initializes a resource buffer through those callbacks, ResourceBufferFreeCleanup releases the buffer through the release slot, allocObjectAndSetFields allocates a 28-byte object through the +0x20 slot and fills five caller-supplied fields, IndirectCallDispatch is the generic release-slot dispatch helper and AllocatorFreeWrapper forwards to sub_58AA6F. The shared layout is evidenced at different bases across call sites (this, a2, a5); merging them is an inference from the consistent callback pattern and is not proven common ownership.

classes.name: CMpegBase
classes.responsibility: Synthetic grouping of the MPEG audio bitstream/header-processing helpers that delegate to the shared callee CMpegBase_ProcessHeader (0x0052DA30): a frame-header decode with bit-position bookkeeping, a word read through a vtable I/O interface, and a next-sync-word predicate. The 'this' object carries the bitstream buffer pointer (+0x24A4), the bit position snapshot and position (+0x24A8/+0x24AC), the frame size in bytes (+0x2498), a default header word (+0x24F0) and an I/O interface pointer (+0x2D34) whose vtable slot +8 is a read function. The class boundary is inferred from the shared fields and callee; ownership is UNKNOWN and the Network* ABI leads are LEGACY-trust naming, not proof of a network class.

The boundary is inferred from the shared zlib inflate context and the callee relationship; owners are UNKNOWN and the inflate/stream struct layouts are caller-defined.

classes.name: ZlibDeflateCompression
classes.responsibility: Synthetic grouping of the DEFLATE compression-side helpers: the hash-chain longest-match search, the Huffman tree constructor, the maximum-length rank redistribution (gen_bitlen equivalent) and the canonical code assignment (gen_codes equivalent). The shared descriptor ('this') carries the symbol frequency table base (+0x0), the maximum symbol index (+0x4), a tree-state block pointer (+0x8) and the symbol count (+0x14). The zlib interpretation is DERIVED from the structural match to deflate and the callee names; owners are UNKNOWN and the deeper state-object roles are not independently proven.

classes.name: SmallBoundByteArray
classes.responsibility: A tiny fixed-size byte array exposed as a __thiscall receiver with a single bounds-checked byte store (index <= 8), used by BufferInitZero to fill individual bytes of a small buffer without allowing out-of-range writes. The enclosing object layout and member semantics are not available from this packet.

classes.name: RuntimeUtility

state_machines.name: InflateFastPathResultState
transitions: Literal symbols (node flag byte zero) write the literal into the output window and stay in the fast path.
Length/distance symbols copy a match from the window and stay in the fast path.
A final literal/length symbol carrying the 0x20 flag completes the block and returns BLOCK_COMPLETE (1).
Window space below 0x102 bytes or buffered input below 0xA bits leaves the fast path and returns NEEDS_SLOW_PATH (0).
A distance node carrying the 0x40 flag writes the 'invalid distance code' string into the stream error slot and returns INVALID_CODE (-3).
A literal/length node carrying the 0x40 flag writes the 'invalid literal/length code' string into the stream error slot and returns INVALID_CODE (-3).

interfaces.name: IoReadInterface
interfaces.purpose: Vtable-based I/O object interface: a read-style function at vtable slot +8 is invoked as (buffer, size, offset) to pull bytes from the I/O object (e.g. a 4-byte word). Only the slot-8 read entry is evidenced; the rest of the vtable and the object identity are unknown.

interfaces.name: AllocationCallbacks
interfaces.purpose: Allocator descriptor contract: an allocation callback at +0x20 (called as alloc(handle, tag, size) returning a pointer or null), a release callback at +0x24 (release(handle, ptr)) and a handle/context dword at +0x28. Realized by the resource-buffer allocation/free helpers and the small-object allocation helper; the exact receiver semantics of each callback are not proven.

compatibility_contracts.name: MPEGHeaderValidationReturnContract
compatibility_contracts.description: CMpegBase_ProcessHeader (0x0052DA30) is used by all three MPEG helpers with a 0/-1 return convention: 0 means a valid header, -1 invalid. NetworkPacketSend returns the same 0/-1, NetworkColorIsDefault returns TRUE exactly when the header is invalid (-1), and BitstreamMpegHeaderDecode only advances the bit position when the result is not -1. A replacement must preserve this return convention and the -1 sentinel meaning.

compatibility_contracts.name: MPEGFrameBitAdvanceContract
compatibility_contracts.description: On a valid frame header BitstreamMpegHeaderDecode snapshots the bit position to this+0x24A8 and advances the position at this+0x24AC by 8 * frame_size_bytes(this+0x2498) + 32 bits. A replacement must reproduce this bit accounting so subsequent frame reads stay aligned to the stream.

compatibility_contracts.name: InflateFastPathHandoffContract
compatibility_contracts.description: InflateFastDecode is entered only when the output window has at least 0x102 bytes free and the input has at least 0xA bits buffered; it returns 1 (block complete), 0 (needs the slow path / more input or window space) or -3 (invalid code) and persists the bit accumulator, bit count, input pointer/counters and output cursor into the inflate context a5 and stream a6. A replacement decoder must preserve this entry precondition, the state-persist handoff and the invalid-code error-string behavior.

compatibility_contracts.name: AllocationCallbackContract
compatibility_contracts.description: The allocator descriptor exposes allocate at +0x20 (called with handle, tag and size, returning a pointer or null) and release at +0x24 (handle, pointer). ResourceBufferAllocInit returns 0 and frees already-allocated blocks through release on any allocation failure, and ResourceBufferFreeCleanup releases in order the variable buffer, the secondary buffer, then the struct itself. A replacement allocator must honor the null-return-on-failure and the release order.

compatibility_contracts.name: Adler32ChecksumContract
compatibility_contracts.description: The checksum routine implements standard Adler-32: the seed is a rolling pair (s1 low 16 bits, s2 high 16 bits), input is processed in chunks of at most 5552 (NMAX) bytes with per-chunk modulo-65521 reduction of both sums, and the result is s1 | (s2 << 16). A replacement must match the chunking and modulus to reproduce identical checksums.
